title: Envisioning emerging technology for 2012 and beyond
author: Michell Zappa (Envisioning Technology)
frame: Vertical timeline 2012-2040, one node per technology per year, plus a quantitative-forecasts column. A node between two year lines is read as the later year.
quote: Looking at emerging trends and research, one can predict and draw conclusions about how the technological sphere is developing, and which technologies should become mainstream in the coming years.

entries.label: High-frequency trading
entries.note: Node sits in the top band, above the 2012 line (read as 2012).
entries.interpretation: Automated, algorithmic high-frequency trading as a standard, dominant practice in equity markets.
entries.verdict_reason: Test: professional practice. HFT became the dominant source of US equity volume around 2008-2009 (Tabb estimates of 50-70% of volume by 2009-2010), and HFT revenues had already peaked in 2009. That puts mainstream status about 3 years before the placed year 2012. The early-forecast rule puts 3-5 years early in partial. Hit would need mainstream arrival within 2010-2014; the take-off came before that window.

evidence.title: Equity Market Structure Literature Review Part II: High Frequency Trading (SEC staff)
evidence.shows: SEC staff review cites industry estimates that HFT accounted for roughly half or more of US equity volume by the late 2000s.

evidence.title: High-frequency trading (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Summarizes Tabb Group data: HFT was 73% of US equity order volume in 2009 and 56% of equity trades in 2010, with revenues falling from $7.2bn in 2009 to $1.8bn in 2012.

entries.label: Cloud computing
entries.note: Node sits in the top band, above the 2012 line (read as 2012).
entries.interpretation: On-demand, pay-as-you-go computing, storage and software delivered over the internet (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS).
entries.verdict_reason: Professional test. By 2012 AWS served hundreds of thousands of business and government customers in 190 countries, and S3 held 1.3 trillion objects. The 2013 RightScale survey found 75% of organizations already used cloud to some extent. Cloud was standard practice in IT at the placed year, so the distance is 0 years. Consumer cloud services (webmail, online storage) were also widespread by then.

evidence.title: Amazon Web Services Announces First Global Customer and Partner Conference, AWS re:Invent
evidence.shows: AWS powered hundreds of thousands of enterprise, government and startup customers in 190 countries in 2012.

evidence.title: Amazon's S3 Now Stores Over 1.3 Trillion Objects
evidence.shows: S3 stored 1.3 trillion objects and handled over 830,000 requests per second in late 2012.

evidence.title: RightScale State of the Cloud Report 2013
evidence.shows: About 75% of surveyed organizations used cloud to some extent in early 2013.

entries.label: Multi touch
entries.note: Node sits in the top band, above the 2012 line (read as 2012).
entries.interpretation: Multi-touch touchscreens as the standard interface on mass-market consumer devices (smartphones, tablets).
entries.verdict_reason: Test: consumer feature shipped as standard on mass-market devices. Capacitive multi-touch became the default smartphone interface after the 2007 iPhone and Android, and Pew measured 46% of US adults owning a smartphone in early 2012. The 10% threshold was crossed around 2010, within 2 years of 2012, so the forecast was on time rather than late. Hit, not partial, because mainstream status and the placed year coincide.

evidence.title: Nearly half of American adults are smartphone owners
evidence.shows: 46% of US adults owned a smartphone in February 2012, up from 35% in May 2011.

evidence.title: Smartphone Ownership Update: September 2012
evidence.shows: More US adults owned smartphones than feature phones by 2012.

entries.label: Depth imaging
entries.note: Node sits in the top band, above the 2012 line (read as 2012).
entries.interpretation: Cameras that capture per-pixel depth (structured light, time-of-flight) in consumer devices.
entries.verdict_reason: Kinect brought consumer depth imaging to market in 2010 and reached 24 million units by February 2013, but it was an optional console peripheral, about one per three Xbox 360s, and Microsoft discontinued it in 2017. That is real but niche adoption against the consumer test (10%+ of households or a standard feature on mass-market devices). Depth sensing became a standard feature on mass-market devices with the iPhone X TrueDepth camera in late 2017, 5 years after 2012. Both routes give partial, not hit.

evidence.title: Kinect sales reach 24 million
evidence.shows: Kinect reached 24 million units against 76 million Xbox 360 consoles, a peripheral share, not a household standard.

evidence.title: A closer look at the capabilities and risks of iPhone X face mapping
evidence.shows: Depth imaging shipped as a standard front-camera feature on a mass-market phone in November 2017.

entries.label: Tablets
entries.note: Node sits in the top band, above the 2012 line (read as 2012).
entries.interpretation: Tablet computers (iPad class) owned by a large share of consumers.
entries.verdict_reason: Consumer test. Pew measured 25% of US adults owning a tablet in August 2012 and 34% in May 2013. The threshold of roughly 10% was crossed in 2011-2012, which is inside the placed year. This is a hit, not early, because ownership was still below 10% when the iPad launched in 2010.

evidence.title: 25% of American Adults Own Tablet Computers | Pew Research Center
evidence.shows: A quarter of US adults owned a tablet in 2012, the placed year.

evidence.title: Tablet Ownership 2013 | Pew Research Center
evidence.shows: Tablet ownership rose to 34% of US adults by May 2013.

entries.label: Rapid personal gene sequencing
entries.claim: Rapid personal gene sequencing becomes mainstream around 2012
entries.note: Node sits in the top band, above the 2012 line (read as 2012).
entries.interpretation: Fast, affordable whole-genome sequencing of individuals, for consumers or as routine clinical care.
entries.verdict_reason: Test: consumer product (10%+ of people) or routine clinical practice. In 2012 physician-ordered and consumer whole-genome sequencing existed as a real but tiny commercial service; the $1,000 genome only arrived with Illumina HiSeq X in 2014. By 2019 Veritas, a leading consumer WGS provider, had sequenced about 5,000 genomes, while 26 million people had bought cheaper genotyping (not sequencing). It is not mainstream within 5 years of 2012, so this is partial only on the niche-adoption clause; it is close to a miss.

evidence.title: Illumina announces $1000 whole human genome sequencing machine
evidence.shows: The $1,000 whole-genome price point arrived only in 2014, two years after the placed year, and on large institutional machines.

evidence.title: 23andMe competitor Veritas Genetics slashes price of whole genome sequencing 40% to $600
evidence.shows: Veritas had sequenced only about 5,000 consumer genomes by 2019; consumers were slow to move from genotyping to whole-genome sequencing.

evidence.title: More than 26 million people have taken an at-home ancestry test
evidence.shows: Mass consumer uptake was genotyping arrays, not sequencing.

entries.label: Additive manufacturing
entries.note: Node sits in the top band, above the 2012 line (read as 2012).
entries.interpretation: 3D printing / additive manufacturing used as a normal production method in industry and in homes.
entries.verdict_reason: Industrial test. AM was real and routine for prototyping by 2012, but the whole industry was only $2.2 billion that year. By 2023 it reached about $20 billion, still a very small fraction of global manufacturing, and consumer 3D printers did not reach 10% of households. AM was real but niche at the placed year and is still not mainstream production practice 5+ years later. Partial for real niche adoption; not a hit because production use never became standard across manufacturing.

evidence.title: Wohlers Report 2013 Reveals Continued Growth in 3D Printing and Additive Manufacturing
evidence.shows: The global AM market for products and services was $2.204 billion in 2012.

evidence.title: 3D Printing Industry hits new high at $20 billion according to Wohlers Report 2024
evidence.shows: The AM industry reached about $20 billion in 2023, small against total manufacturing output.

entries.label: Global online population: ± 2 billion
entries.note: Text block sits in the 2012 row of the quantitative forecasts panel.
entries.interpretation: About 2 billion people use the internet in 2012.
entries.verdict_reason: Quantitative test (D10: hit within 10%, partial within 25%). ITU counted 2.3 billion internet users at end-2011 and over 2.7 billion in 2013, so 2012 sits near 2.5 billion. The poster figure of 2 billion is about 20% low. That is inside 25% and outside 10%, so partial.

evidence.title: Measuring the Information Society 2012 (ITU)
evidence.shows: About a third of the world population, 2.3 billion people, was online at end-2011.

evidence.title: ICT Facts and Figures 2013 (ITU)
evidence.shows: Over 2.7 billion people used the internet in 2013, which puts 2012 near 2.5 billion.

entries.label: Connected devices: ±10 billion
entries.note: Text block sits in the 2012 row of the quantitative forecasts panel.
entries.interpretation: About 10 billion devices are connected to the internet in 2012.
entries.verdict_reason: Quantitative test. Estimates for 2012 disagree because the definition of a connected device varies. Cisco put internet-connected devices at 8.7 billion in 2012; IDATE counted 15 billion connected machines and objects. Against Cisco the poster is about 15% high (partial); against IDATE it is 33% low (miss). Partial on the lower, internet-connected count, which matches the poster's wording.

evidence.title: How Many Things Are Currently Connected To The Internet of Things (IoT)? (Forbes/Quora)
evidence.shows: Cites Cisco's figure of 8.7 billion internet-connected devices in 2012, with other estimates in the 8 to 10 billion range.

evidence.title: Internet of Things market tripled to 15 bln devices in 2012 (Telecompaper, IDATE study)
evidence.shows: IDATE counted 15 billion connected machines, devices and objects in 2012, a wider definition.

entries.label: Inductive chargers
entries.note: Node sits between the 2012 and 2013 lines (read as 2013).
entries.interpretation: Inductive (Qi-type) wireless charging as a standard feature for phones and other consumer devices.
entries.verdict_reason: Test: shipped as standard on mass-market devices. In 2013 Qi existed on a few phones (Nexus 4/5, some Lumias): real but niche. It became a standard flagship feature only with the Galaxy S8 and iPhone 8 in 2017, when about 500 million wireless-charging devices shipped. That is 4 years after 2013, so partial on both the niche and the distance criteria. Not a hit because 2013 adoption was far below mass-market level.

evidence.title: IHS Markit: half a billion devices with wireless power shipped in 2017
evidence.shows: Wireless-charging device shipments rose 40% in 2017, driven by the Galaxy S8 and iPhone 8/X adding the feature.

evidence.title: Qi (standard)
evidence.shows: Timeline of Qi adoption across phone makers, with Apple joining in 2017.

entries.label: World population: 7 billion
entries.note: Text block sits in the 2013 row of the quantitative forecasts panel.
entries.interpretation: World population is about 7 billion in 2013.
entries.verdict_reason: Quantitative test. The UN estimated world population at 7.2 billion in mid-2013. The poster figure of 7 billion is about 3% low, inside the 10% hit margin. The UN had marked the 7 billion day in October 2011, so the placement is slightly late but the number for 2013 is within tolerance.

evidence.title: World population projected to reach 9.6 billion by 2050 (UN News)
evidence.shows: The UN 2012 Revision puts world population at 7.2 billion in mid-2013.

entries.label: Software agents
entries.note: Node centre sits on the 2014 line.
entries.interpretation: Software assistants that act for the user on requests and context (Siri, Google Now, Cortana class), not full autonomous agents.
entries.verdict_reason: Siri shipped in 2011, Google Now in 2012 and Cortana in April 2014, so by 2014 every major smartphone OS shipped a built-in assistant agent as a standard feature (consumer test, standard feature on mass-market devices). Pew found nearly half of US adults used a voice assistant by 2017. Mainstream status falls in 2012-2014, within 2 years of 2014. If the label means autonomous goal-directed agents, that arrived only around 2025 and would be a miss; I read the 2012 label as the assistant class.

evidence.title: Beyond Siri, Google Now and Cortana: The Future of Virtual Assistants
evidence.shows: In 2014 all three major mobile platforms shipped a built-in assistant agent.

evidence.title: Nearly half of Americans use digital voice assistants, mostly on their smartphones
evidence.shows: 46% of US adults used a digital assistant by 2017, mostly on phones.

entries.label: Cyber-warfare
entries.note: Node centre sits on the 2014 line.
entries.interpretation: State-sponsored cyber attacks used as instruments of conflict, routinely occurring and reported as normal.
entries.verdict_reason: Abstract-practice test. Stuxnet (2010) was a single early case. By 2014-2017 state cyber attacks were routine news: the FBI attributed the Sony Pictures attack to North Korea in December 2014, attacks hit the Ukrainian grid in 2015-2016, and NotPetya followed in 2017. Routine occurrence starts within 2 years of 2014, so this is a hit.

evidence.title: FBI Says North Korea Was Behind Sony Hack
evidence.shows: The US government publicly attributed a destructive cyber attack to a nation state in the placed year.

evidence.title: Five notorious cyberattacks that targeted governments
evidence.shows: Lists Stuxnet (2010) and NotPetya (2017) among a series of state-linked attacks, showing the practice became recurrent in the 2010s.

entries.label: Gesture recognition
entries.note: Node sits between the 2013 and 2014 lines (read as 2014).
entries.interpretation: Touchless body/hand gesture recognition as an input method for consumer devices (camera-based, Kinect-style).
entries.verdict_reason: Test: consumer feature on mass-market devices. Kinect reached 24 million units by February 2013, close to the placed year 2014, but it was an add-on to one console line and never became a standard input on mass-market devices. Microsoft ended Kinect manufacturing in October 2017 and touchless gesture input did not replace it. Real adoption that then faded fits partial better than hit; it is not a miss because tens of millions of households used it around the placed year.

evidence.title: Kinect sales reach 24 million
evidence.shows: Microsoft reported 24 million Kinect sensors sold against 76 million Xbox 360 consoles by February 2013.

evidence.title: Microsoft ceases production of the Kinect
evidence.shows: Microsoft stopped manufacturing the consumer Kinect in 2017, so camera gesture input did not stay a mainstream consumer feature.

entries.label: Near-field communication
entries.note: Node sits between the 2013 and 2014 lines (read as 2014).
entries.interpretation: NFC radios as a standard smartphone feature used for contactless payment and tap interactions.
entries.verdict_reason: Consumer test (standard feature on mass-market devices). NFC shipped in 18% of 1.5 billion phones in 2013 and IHS expected 416 million NFC phones in 2014. Apple added NFC and Apple Pay to the iPhone 6 in September 2014, which made NFC standard on both major smartphone platforms. Mainstream falls at 2014 to 2016, within 2 years of the placed year.

evidence.title: Two in three phones to come with NFC in 2018
evidence.shows: IHS data: NFC was in 18.2% of phones shipped in 2013 and NFC phone shipments were set to grow above 50% to 416 million in 2014.

evidence.title: Apple Announces Apple Pay
evidence.shows: Apple shipped NFC-based Apple Pay on iPhone 6 and iPhone 6 Plus from October 2014.

entries.label: Volumetric (3D) screens
entries.note: Node centre sits on the 2014 line.
entries.interpretation: Reading: 3D displays in general, counting consumer stereoscopic 3D TVs as the claim's subject (per the 2011 '3D screens and cameras' label); true volumetric displays are the strict reading.
entries.verdict_reason: Test: consumer feature shipped on mass-market devices. 3D-capable TVs reached about 20% of global flat-panel TV sales in 2013, but the feature sat on premium sets, actual usage stayed low, and Samsung, Sony, LG and others dropped 3D by 2016-2017. That is real but niche use around 2014 followed by abandonment, so partial under the lenient reading. Under the strict reading (true volumetric displays) the verdict is a clear miss: no volumetric display ever reached consumers.

evidence.title: 3D TV Sales Up 8.3% in 2013
evidence.shows: 3D TVs were about 20.6% of global flat-panel TV sales in 2013 (DisplaySearch).

evidence.title: 3D TVs are dead
evidence.shows: Major TV makers stopped supporting 3D by 2016-2017 because usage was low.

entries.label: Appliance robots
entries.note: Node centre sits on the 2014 line.
entries.interpretation: Single-purpose home robots such as robot vacuums and mops.
entries.verdict_reason: In 2014 robot vacuums were a real niche: iRobot had sold about 10 million Roombas cumulatively by 2013, and iRobot's own filings still called global household penetration single digits in 2018. US household ownership now sits near 20-25%, so the 10% line in rich markets was crossed around 2019-2020, 5-6 years after 2014. Real but niche adoption by 2014 gives partial; the late crossing rules out hit.

evidence.title: iRobot Corp Form 10-K FY2018
evidence.shows: iRobot described robotic vacuum household penetration as still low, in the single digits, in 2018.

evidence.title: iRobot Corp Form 10-K FY2013
evidence.shows: Robot vacuums were an established commercial product line by the placed year.

entries.label: Self-healing materials
entries.note: Node centre sits on the 2014 line.
entries.interpretation: Materials that repair damage autonomously, used in mainstream products.
entries.verdict_reason: Industrial/consumer test. As of 2024-2025, reviews and IDTechEx describe most self-healing technologies as developmental or early commercial, with niche use in coatings, some phone back covers and tires. They are not standard practice in any major field by 2019 (placed year + 5) or today. This is a miss, not a niche-based partial, because in 2014 the products were demonstrations and isolated items, not real adoption.

evidence.title: Automotive: The Road to Commercialization of Self-Healing Materials | IDTechEx
evidence.shows: Self-healing materials were still on the road to commercialization in 2025.

evidence.title: Practical Applications of Self-Healing Polymers Beyond Mechanical and Electrical Recovery - Advanced Science
evidence.shows: Peer-reviewed review states scalability and robustness problems have limited commercialization.

entries.label: Speech recognition
entries.note: Node centre sits on the 2015 line.
entries.interpretation: Voice/speech recognition as an everyday input on consumer devices (voice assistants, dictation, voice search).
entries.verdict_reason: Test: consumer feature. Siri (2011) and Google voice search shipped speech recognition as a standard smartphone feature in the early 2010s, and in May 2017 Pew found 46% of US adults used voice assistants. Mass use arrived in the 2013-2017 range, within 2 years of the placed year 2015.

evidence.title: Nearly half of Americans use digital voice assistants, mostly on their smartphones
evidence.shows: 46% of US adults used voice assistants in 2017, 42% on smartphones.

entries.label: Pervasive video capture
entries.claim: Pervasive video capture becomes mainstream around 2015
entries.note: Node centre sits on the 2015 line.
entries.interpretation: Reading: society-wide, near-constant video recording of public and private life (phone cameras, CCTV, police body cams, dashcams), not only wearable lifelogging cameras.
entries.verdict_reason: Abstract-practice test. By 2015, 68% of US adults owned a camera smartphone, and by 2016 47% of US general-purpose law enforcement agencies and 80% of large departments had body-worn cameras. Continuous video capture was routine and reported as normal around the placed year (distance 0 to 1 years). If the label is read narrowly as always-on wearable lifelogging cameras (Narrative Clip, Google Glass), the verdict would be miss, because that category failed.

evidence.title: Body-Worn Cameras in Law Enforcement Agencies, 2016
evidence.shows: 47% of US general-purpose law enforcement agencies and 80% of large police departments had acquired body-worn cameras in 2016.

evidence.title: U.S. Technology Device Ownership 2015
evidence.shows: 68% of US adults owned a smartphone in 2015, up from 35% in 2011.

entries.label: Tidal turbines
entries.note: Node sits between the 2014 and 2015 lines (read as 2015).
entries.interpretation: Tidal stream turbines as a material share of new electricity generating capacity.
entries.verdict_reason: Test: energy, material share of new capacity. Tidal stream was at demonstration scale in 2015; the largest array, MeyGen phase 1, is 6 MW (first power November 2016). Europe had about 32 MW cumulative tidal stream installed by 2024, a negligible share of capacity. Not mainstream within 5 years of 2015 or since. Demonstration plants do not qualify as niche adoption under the energy test, so miss, not partial.

evidence.title: Ocean Energy Stats & Trends 2024
evidence.shows: Only about 130 kW of tidal stream was deployed in Europe in 2024; cumulative capacity is tens of MW.

evidence.title: MeyGen
evidence.shows: The world's largest tidal stream array has 6 MW installed, first power in 2016.

entries.label: Global online population: ± 2.5 billion
entries.note: Text block sits in the 2015 row of the quantitative forecasts panel.
entries.interpretation: About 2.5 billion people use the internet in 2015.
entries.verdict_reason: Quantitative test. ITU counted 3.2 billion internet users in 2015. The poster figure of 2.5 billion is about 22% low: inside 25%, outside 10%, so partial. The poster underestimated internet growth.

evidence.title: ICT Facts and Figures 2015 (ITU)
evidence.shows: 3.2 billion people used the internet in 2015, 43% of world population.

entries.label: Connected devices: ±15 billion
entries.note: Text block sits in the 2015 row of the quantitative forecasts panel.
entries.interpretation: About 15 billion devices are connected in 2015.
entries.verdict_reason: Quantitative test. The Ericsson Mobility Report of November 2015 counted about 15 billion connected devices in 2015 (phones, PCs, tablets, consumer electronics, M2M and fixed phones). The poster figure matches within 10%, so hit. Ericsson counts mobile subscriptions as devices; a narrower count would be lower.

evidence.title: Ericsson Mobility Report, November 2015
evidence.shows: The connected-devices chart gives 15 billion connected devices in 2015 and 28 billion forecast for 2021.

entries.label: Natural language interpretation
entries.claim: Natural language interpretation becomes mainstream around 2016
entries.note: Node centre sits on the 2016 line.
entries.interpretation: Machines that understand spoken or written natural language well enough for everyday use (voice assistants, machine translation).
entries.verdict_reason: In 2016 Google switched Translate to neural machine translation and launched Google Assistant, while Alexa devices spread. Pew found 46% of US adults used voice assistants in 2017 and 25% owned a smart speaker by 2019. Natural language interfaces were a standard feature on mass-market phones and speakers in 2016-2018, within 2 years of 2016 (consumer test).

evidence.title: A Neural Network for Machine Translation, at Production Scale
evidence.shows: Google put neural language interpretation into a mass-market product in 2016.

evidence.title: Nearly half of Americans use digital voice assistants, mostly on their smartphones
evidence.shows: 46% of US adults used voice assistants in 2017.

evidence.title: Americans and their smart speakers: 5 findings about their views and habits
evidence.shows: A quarter of US adults had a smart speaker in 2019.

entries.label: 4G
entries.note: Node sits between the 2015 and 2016 lines (read as 2016).
entries.interpretation: 4G/LTE mobile networks widely deployed and used by a large share of subscribers.
entries.verdict_reason: Infrastructure test. Ericsson counted 1 billion LTE subscriptions at end-2015 and reported LTE becoming the dominant global access technology in 2017-2018. In rich markets (US, Korea, Japan) LTE was already the majority by 2015-2016. Mainstream falls within 2 years of 2016, so this is a hit.

evidence.title: Ericsson Mobility Report June 2016
evidence.shows: About one billion LTE subscriptions existed worldwide at end of 2015.

evidence.title: Ericsson Mobility Report November 2017
evidence.shows: LTE was set to become the dominant mobile access technology around 2017-2018.

entries.label: Flexible screens
entries.note: Node sits between the 2015 and 2016 lines (read as 2016).
entries.interpretation: Flexible (plastic-substrate) display panels shipping in consumer devices, not only foldables.
entries.verdict_reason: Test: standard feature on mass-market devices. Flexible AMOLED smartphone panel shipments rose from 40 million in 2016 to 125 million in 2017, driven by iPhone X and Samsung Galaxy flagships. Flexible panels became standard on flagship phones in 2016-2018, within 2 years of 2016. Foldable form factors stay niche, but the label is about flexible screens, which shipped at scale.

evidence.title: AMOLED Panel Demand in Smartphone Market Expected to Grow Much Slower Than Expected, IHS Markit Says
evidence.shows: IHS Markit reported film-based flexible AMOLED smartphone panel shipments tripled to 125 million in 2017 from 40 million in 2016.

entries.label: Telematics
entries.note: Node sits between the 2015 and 2016 lines (read as 2016).
entries.interpretation: Vehicle telematics: embedded cellular connectivity and remote data exchange in cars and fleets (connected-car data, emergency call, tracking).
entries.verdict_reason: Consumer test (standard feature on mass-market vehicles). The EU made eCall, an embedded telematics unit, mandatory in all new car and van models from 31 March 2018. Counterpoint reported that over half of cars sold globally in 2020 were connected. Telematics became a standard feature between 2016 and 2020; the core shift lands within 2 years of 2016 (EU mandate 2018).

evidence.title: Saving lives: eCall mandatory in new car models from this week
evidence.shows: All new EU car and light-van models must carry the eCall telematics system from 31 March 2018.

evidence.title: Podcast: Over 50% of Cars Sold Globally in 2020 will be Connected
evidence.shows: Counterpoint estimated that more than half of new cars sold globally in 2020 had embedded connectivity.

entries.label: Organ printing
entries.note: Node sits between the 2015 and 2016 lines (read as 2016).
entries.interpretation: 3D bioprinting of transplantable functional organs as clinical practice.
entries.verdict_reason: Test: medical, standard practice. As of 2025 reviews, no bioprinted solid organ has been transplanted as routine care; the field is in research and early clinical trials of simple tissues. Printed anatomical models for surgical planning exist but are not organ printing. Not mainstream within 5 years of 2016 (by 2021) or since, so miss.

evidence.title: Advances and Challenges in 3D Bioprinting for Organ Transplantation
evidence.shows: Clinical use faces scale-up, vascularization, immune and regulatory barriers; full organ transplantation remains a future goal.

evidence.title: Engineering the future of organ transplantation: A comprehensive review of 3D bioprinting advances
evidence.shows: Review frames bioprinted organs as still under development.

entries.label: Fuel cells
entries.note: Node sits between the 2015 and 2016 lines (read as 2016).
entries.interpretation: Fuel cells as a mainstream energy technology in vehicles, stationary power or consumer devices.
entries.verdict_reason: In 2016 global fuel cell vehicle sales were in the low thousands (Mirai about 2,000 worldwide) and total fuel cell shipments were a few hundred megawatts, a rounding error against global power and vehicle markets. Shipments passed 1 GW only in 2019, still far from a material share of new capacity (energy test). Fuel cells stayed niche through 2021 and remain niche now; battery EVs took the vehicle role.

evidence.title: Fuel Cell Technologies Market Report 2016 (US DOE)
evidence.shows: DOE market data for 2016 show fuel cells as a small, early-commercial market.

evidence.title: Fact of the Month 17-01: Cumulative US sales of fuel cell vehicles totaled 2,748
evidence.shows: Cumulative US fuel cell car sales were under 3,000 units by late 2016.

entries.label: Commercial spaceflight
entries.note: Node sits between the 2015 and 2016 lines (read as 2016).
entries.interpretation: Private companies routinely flying payloads and people to space as a commercial service.
entries.verdict_reason: Industry test. Commercial cargo flights to the ISS (SpaceX Dragon) ran from 2012, so real but niche commercial activity existed by 2016. Commercial crew became routine only after Crew Dragon Demo-2 in May 2020, and private tourist flights (Blue Origin, Virgin Galactic, Inspiration4) started in 2021, 4-5 years after the placed year. Space tourism remains a few hundred people, so no reading makes this a hit; the niche 2016 activity and 2020 crew routine make it partial, not miss.

evidence.title: SpaceX Demo 2 Mission Launches into History - NASA
evidence.shows: The first crewed orbital flight on a commercial spacecraft came in 2020, four years after the placed year.

evidence.title: SpaceX Inspiration4 mission sent 4 people with minimal training into orbit
evidence.shows: Private tourist spaceflight began in 2021 and was still described as coming closer to reality, not mainstream.

entries.label: Mesh networking
entries.note: Node sits between the 2016 and 2017 lines (read as 2017).
entries.interpretation: Mesh networking in consumer and home networks (mesh Wi-Fi systems, plus smart-home mesh such as Thread/Zigbee).
entries.verdict_reason: Test: consumer product at roughly 10%+ of households. Consumer mesh Wi-Fi launched in 2016 (eero, Google Wifi). Parks Associates found 11% of US broadband households had a mesh Wi-Fi product in 2019, and 32% of US internet households in 2025. The 10% threshold was crossed about 2019, 2 years after the placed year 2017, so it is a hit at the edge of the window.

evidence.title: 22% of US broadband households have a Wi-Fi network extender and 11% have a Wi-Fi mesh networking product
evidence.shows: 11% of US broadband households owned mesh Wi-Fi in 2019.

evidence.title: Vast majority (80%) of US households have a home network router; 28% report intentions to purchase
evidence.shows: Parks Associates 2025 home-network data; search summaries of this release series report mesh ownership at 32% of US internet households (figure not confirmed on this exact page).

entries.label: Augmented reality
entries.note: Node sits between the 2016 and 2017 lines (read as 2017).
entries.interpretation: Digital content overlaid on the live camera view or the real world, on phones or headsets.
entries.verdict_reason: Consumer test (standard feature on mass-market devices). Pokemon Go reached more than 500 million downloads in 2016. Apple shipped ARKit in iOS 11 in 2017 to hundreds of millions of iPhones and iPads, and Google followed with ARCore. Phone-based AR became a standard platform feature at the placed year (distance 0 to 1 years). Headset AR stayed niche, but the label does not require headsets.

evidence.title: Apple's ARKit is Bringing Augmented Reality to "hundreds of millions of iPhones and iPads"
evidence.shows: Apple made AR a standard iOS 11 capability on hundreds of millions of devices in 2017.

evidence.title: Pokemon Go gets better augmented reality thanks to ARKit on iOS
evidence.shows: The mass-market AR game Pokemon Go added ARKit-based AR+ in December 2017.

entries.label: Biometric sensors
entries.note: Node sits between the 2016 and 2017 lines (read as 2017).
entries.interpretation: Biometric sensors (fingerprint, face, heart-rate) as standard features of consumer devices.
entries.verdict_reason: Test: shipped as standard feature on mass-market devices. Fingerprint sensors reached 55-64% of global smartphone shipments in 2017 (TrendForce, Digitimes Research), and 21% of US adults regularly wore a smartwatch or fitness tracker with heart-rate sensing by 2019. Mainstream in 2016-2017, within 2 years of 2017. Hit.

evidence.title: Global fingerprint-enabled smartphone shipments hit 920 million units in 2017
evidence.shows: 920 million fingerprint-enabled smartphones shipped in 2017, a 64% penetration rate.

evidence.title: About one-in-five Americans use a smart watch or fitness tracker
evidence.shows: 21% of US adults regularly wore a smartwatch or fitness tracker in 2019.

entries.label: Boards
entries.note: Node sits between the 2016 and 2017 lines (read as 2017).
